issues.description: The problem statement inconsistently uses two different method names for the animal feeding sound: the UML and tasks require an abstract method messageOnFeed(), but several later sections (including the song template text) refer to getFeedingSound(). This naming mismatch between the specification and the example usage can confuse students about which method to implement and call (e.g., in Farm.feedAllAnimals() and singFarmSong()). The provided solution uses messageOnFeed(), but the ambiguity in the problem text is likely to mislead students.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name throughout the problem statement, template, and examples. Preferably change all occurrences of getFeedingSound() in problem_statement.md and template comments to messageOnFeed(), or alternatively rename the abstract method in the UML and tasks to getFeedingSound() consistently. Update example song text and descriptions to call the same method name students are instructed to implement.

issues.description: The problem statement refers to a feeding-sound method named getFeedingSound() (e.g. for Seal, Pig, Goat), while the UML, template expectations, and the provided solution consistently define and implement an abstract method messageOnFeed(). This naming mismatch (getFeedingSound vs. messageOnFeed) refers to the same conceptual operation (the animal's feeding sound) but uses different identifiers across artifacts and can mislead students about which method to implement or call.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier across artifacts. Replace accidental references to getFeedingSound() in the problem statement with messageOnFeed(), or (less recommended) update the template and solution to use getFeedingSound() consistently. Ensure the wording and the UML/method signatures all use the same method name so students know which method to implement and call.
